business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Wholesale Trade of Aged Scotch and Bordeaux Wines

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – Civil Law (Quebec private law, including partnership and property) and Common Law (federal constitutional, criminal, customs, and public law)

Canada–France Tax Convention (Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement, 1975, as amended)
Canada–United Kingdom Tax Convention (Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement, 1980)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and associated Regulations (SOR/2002-412); Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part II.1 (money laundering and proceeds of crime); Act respecting the Legal Publicity of Enterprises, C.Q.L.R. c. U-2.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Québec notary (notaire en exercice) in the district of the partnership's registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarial act – no consular legalization required for use within Quebec

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and extract of the official company register of the non-resident general partner (including ultimate beneficial owners of the general partner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the issuer is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports and two independent proof-of-address documents (utility bill, bank statement) for each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the partnership or of its general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent public authority or supervised financial institution in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney designating the Quebec attorney for service and, where applicable, a resident agent for customs and excise notifications
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified translation into French of all non-French corporate documents, by a certified translator of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec (OTTIAQ)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Attestation of the certified translator – no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every general partner, limited partner, ultimate beneficial owner, and senior officer against: (i) politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance – domestic, foreign, and international organization PEPs; (ii) the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions list; (iii) Canadian sanctions regulations adopted under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, including the Special Economic Measures (Russia) Regulations, SOR/2014-444; (iv) the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky) list; and (v) the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list for all USD-denominated wire transfers and correspondent banking rails. Enhanced due diligence is required for all non-Canadian PEPs, including source-of-funds verification; screening on formation, at each partnership admission, and continuously via automated watch-list monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (RCEQ) – Registre des entreprises du Québec, available at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, C.Q.L.R. c. C-11, s. 64, and ALPE art. 14, the limited partnership's corporate name must be in French; a version in another language may be registered only where the French-language name is the recognized name and the non-French version is permitted in accordance with s. 64(2) of the Charter. All proposed names must be legible in Latin characters, transliteration of non-Latin trade names is permitted only for foreign trademarks, and the legal designation 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' must be included.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant must first obtain from the Registraire the written reasons within the statutory review process: the declarant may file, within 30 days of notification, a formal written application for review under ALPE s. 36, requesting the Registraire to render a fresh decision. If the review confirms the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) within 60 days of the review decision, pursuant to ALPE s. 37 and the rules of the TAQ. During the pendency of the appeal, an administrative hold may be placed on a newly filed proposed name, but the applicant is advised to file a fresh name-reservation request concurrently so as not to lose priority. Corporate counsel should also verify that the rejected name does not violate ss. 14–24 of ALPE (misleading, discriminatory, or illicit names) and prepare a corrected compliant name prior to lodging the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office. The ALPE requires every enterprise to declare an actual establishment in Quebec (chief establishment or establishment address), and administrative authorities (RACJ, CRA and the Registrar) require a physical presence for service of documents. Moreover, the bonded spirits wholesale activity demands an on-site licensed warehouse or contractual controlled access to a CRA-approved bonded storage facility in Quebec. A virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address may be used only as a supplementary mailing address and may never constitute the registered office for excise or provincial alcohol-licensing purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 75% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection within the first six months of operation, given classification as a medium-risk enhanced AML/CFT sector by FINTRAC and the high excise-control profile of a bonded warehouse for aged Scotch and Bordeaux wines; CRA Excise officers, SQ police, and RACJ inspectors may conduct joint visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2236-2247 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 20, 21, 23, 28 and 33 (registration and updating duties); Regulation respecting the fees payable under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1.1).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar) — online services at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca / entreprisesquebec.ca
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership) filed under s. 20 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Quebec law; partners' contributions (money or property for limited partners; money, property or services for the general partner) are fixed in the partnership agreement. No escrow or blocked capital account is required by statute; however, for bonded wine/spirits trade the CRA/CBSA and the RACJ may require a surety bond or financial security in lieu of escrow.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the General Partner and the initial Limited Partners ratify the formation of [•] Limited Partnership governed by the Civil Code of Quebec (arts. 2236-2247). The General Partner is authorized to subscribe the general partner interest and each Limited Partner is admitted for its respective subscribed capital contribution, per the executed Limited Partnership Agreement. The registered office is fixed at [address], Quebec, and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is instructed to file the declaration of registration. The appointed authorized representatives may operate banking accounts, file statutory returns, and bind the Partnership concerning bonded-warehouse wholesale activities. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Proposed name reservation and conflict/confusion clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — name reservation via the online Entreprises Québec portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the proposed limited partnership name (e.g. 'XXX, Société en commandite / Limited Partnership'); the REQ screens the name against registered enterprises, corporate names and trademarks for confusion and impermissible expressions in accordance with ss. 11-17 and 33 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. The name must not be misleading as to the nature of the enterprise and must not contain restricted words requiring prior approval.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership name and two alternate names
Short description of the intended business activity (ISIC 4632 / NAICS 424820)
Name and address of the prospective general partner (commandité)
Written authorization of the applicant if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion or unlawful expression, submit a corrective name reservation with alternate names within 30 days, or request a discretionary administrative review by the Registraire supported by a search summary; refusals may also be remedied by adding distinctive elements to the firm name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the limited partnership agreement (acte de société en commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The partners themselves; notarial deed recommended (not strictly required) for registration of real property or long-term warehouse lease
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign a written partnership agreement which states expressly that the partnership is a limited partnership, the firm name, the registered office (siège social) in Quebec, the identity of the general partner(s) with exclusive management authority, the list of limited partners and their agreed contributions, the capital accounts, the sharing of profits and losses, the fiscal year, and the duration. Under art. 2236 CCQ a limited partner may contribute only money or property (not services); the general partner may contribute money, property or services. Execute the agreement without delay and preserve original signatures for the REQ and financial institutions.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement (original or certified copy)
Schedule of partners and capital contributions
Registered office address evidenced by signed lease or authorization of the owner
Government-issued identification and proof of residential address for each individual signatory
Corporation extract or certificate for any corporate partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a limited partner's contribution is challenged by creditors as an impermissible contribution of services (art. 2236 CCQ), recharacterize the arrangement as a loan or admit the contribution as money or property by means of an amending clause executed by the partners; failure to cure may expose that limited partner to unlimited liability.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the limited partnership with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — secured online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Déclaration d'immatriculation online within 60 days after the partnership is formed: supply the exact legal name (with the 'Société en commandite' indicator), the head office address in Quebec, the description of the principal activity (NAICS 424820 / ISIC 4632), particulars of the general partner and of the persons authorized as representatives who may bind the partnership, and the mailing address. Pay the prescribed CAD $72 fee online. The REQ issues the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and the certificate of registration, which date-stamps the partnership's opposability towards third parties.
required_dossiers: Declaration of registration form (digital, submitted online)
Name reservation certificate or reserved name number
Extract or certified copy of the limited partnership agreement
Mandate (power of attorney) if filed by a third party
Identification and residential address of the general partner and authorized representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected for incompleteness, the Registraire sends a notice; file a corrective declaration (déclaration modificative) within the statutory delay (normally 30 days) and pay the CAD $18 update fee. A right of administrative review under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, s. 111, is available against a refusal to register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Revenu Quebec and the Canada Revenue Agency (QST, GST/HST, payroll and excise accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (QST and NEQ accounts) and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The NEQ assigned by the REQ is transferred automatically to Revenu Québec; activate the QST account for taxable supplies of goods in Quebec exceeding CAD $30,000 annually and the source-deduction account if employees are hired. Register the partnership with the CRA for the GST/HST account under s. 240 of the Excise Tax Act using a new business number, and file the partnership information return (T5013 federal / TP-600 Quebec) for each fiscal year. Because the activity is bonded wine/spirits wholesale, also submit the Excise Warehouse Licence application under the Excise Act, 2001 to the CRA Excise Duty Program and the CBSA Bonded Warehouse Licence application under the Customs Act (separate licensing stage).
required_dossiers: NEQ and REQ certificate of registration
Limited partnership agreement including the partners' income allocation schedule (s. 96 ITA)
Names, business or social insurance numbers, and addresses of all partners to establish residence and allocation
Mandates of authorized representatives for CRA and Revenu Québec accounts
Schedule of anticipated taxable supplies in Quebec and in Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a Revenu Québec or CRA query concerning beneficial ownership or non-residency of limited partners, respond with a completed partnership allocation schedule and powers of attorney within 30 days. Late registrations attract penalties under s. 280 of the Excise Tax Act; these can be reduced or abated through the CRA Voluntary Disclosures Program.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the partnership bank account and constitution of statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered bank or credit union operating in the Province of Quebec (Schedule I bank recommended)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the certificate of registration (NEQ), the signed partnership agreement, partner identification, and an authorization resolution of the general partner naming the signing officers; instruct the bank that the account is opened under the partnership's name with the 'Limited Partnership' denomination and establish the mandatory signing combinations for withdrawals and wire transfers (two-signature rule recommended for the bonded trade's SWIFT wires). The registered office must maintain the registry of partners and minutes of compulsory partner decisions. No escrow account is required by law; however, a separate segregated account for excise duty settlements should be agreed at the bank mandate stage.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration issued by REQ (NEQ)
Limited partnership agreement (certified copy)
Government-issued photo identification of each partner and authorized person
Partner or management resolution appointing the account signatories
Proof of registered office address (invoice or lease)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional documentation for a partnership (e.g., a notarized certificate), obtain a notarial collation of signatures or a certificate of authorized representatives from REQ. If the account opening is declined for KYC/AML reasons, engage another financial institution; no public registry fee is affected by a bank refusal.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business.html); Provincial: Revenu Québec (https://www.revenuquebec.ca) which administers Quebec Sales Tax (QST), corporate/partnership filings, and coordinates with the Registraire des entreprises for the Enterprise Number (NEQ). Customs matters fall under the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign Limited Partnership must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and the associated GST/HST program account (RT) by filing Form RC1 or registering online through the CRA's Business Registration Online, using the non-resident partnership registration flow. If the LP has a place of business or employees in Quebec, it must concurrently register with the Registraire des entreprises for a NEQ (Quebec enterprise number) and then register with Revenu Québec for QST and source-deduction accounts. For bonded wine/spirits trade, the LP must also obtain a CBSA importer/exporter identifier (RM account), a licensed excise warehouse permit under the Excise Act, 2001, and a Quebec liquor permit from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux. A foreign LP without Canadian permanent establishment may nonetheless register voluntarily for GST/HST and QST to claim input tax credits on pre-export purchases, and must file an RC372 election if part of a corporate group.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime; the LP is fiscally transparent under Income Tax Act (ITA) section 96, with income computed at the partnership level and allocated to partners for inclusion in each partner's own return. Available elections include: (1) partnership fiscal period end election under ITA 249.1; (2) mandatory/elective allocation rules for non-resident partners electing under ITA 216 to file on net taxable income instead of Part XIII withholding; (3) joint election under ETA 273 for closely related entities to treat supplies as non-supplies (rarely applicable to an LP); and (4) the RC372 election for GST/HST groups when the LP is a member of a qualifying group. Hybrid mismatch rules under ITA 18.4-18.6 and ETA overriding provisions apply, with no separate election available to neutralize cross-border payment-timing mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) administered jointly in Quebec
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold over a consecutive four-calendar-quarter period for both GST/HST and QST; registration is mandatory once a non-resident LP makes taxable supplies in Canada above this threshold, but voluntary registration is advisable for exporters claiming input tax refunds on inputs used in zero-rated export supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping regime. E-invoicing is voluntary under the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing National Standard (PEPPOL-bis BIS 3.0) adopted in 2022; however, CRA and Revenu Québec require that all invoices contain specified data fields (ETA section 3 and QST rules), including BN, transaction date, clear description, amount and tax calculation, and be preserved in original format for six years. For bonded warehouse withdrawals to export, CBSA requires prior electronic ACI/eManifest filings for goods leaving Canada by road, rail, air, or marine modes, and the CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) platform processes the export declarations digitally via API or portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of wine and spirits qualifies for zero-rated treatment under Schedule VI, Part V, section 1 of the Excise Tax Act where the LP exports the goods in accordance with the ETA export evidence rules: the goods must be supplied to a buyer outside Canada, be safely exported within 60 days of the invoice date (or a longer period allowed by the Minister), and the LP must obtain documentary evidence within two years of the supply. The bonded warehouse transfer itself is not a taxable supply; duty is suspended on the Excise Duty (Excise Act, 2001) and the Quebec specific tax on alcohol until export, provided the transfer is made directly from the licensed bonded warehouse to the export carrier. Zero-rating also covers offshore back-to-back sales where title passes outside Canada and goods are shipped directly from the bonded warehouse to a foreign destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A form) or CARM electronic export declaration showing commodity code 2208, Canadian exporter account, port of exit, and destination country
Bill of Lading (airway bill or sea waybill) issued by the carrier with the bonded warehouse premises as point of loading and a foreign port or airport as destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 wire instruction evidencing currency settlement from the foreign buyer to the LP's Canadian bank account within the applicable repatriation period
Bonded Warehouse Withdrawal Certificate signed by the licensed warehouse keeper under the Excise Act, 2001 confirming duty-suspended removal
SAQ/RACJ endorsement or Quebec liquor permit export rider authorizing the removal of wine and spirits to a foreign consignee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years of an assessment, extended to ten years for misrepresentation; any zero-rating claim lacking adequate export evidence is fully reversed, with net tax reassessed, interest charged at the prescribed rate plus a 6% arrears penalty under ETA section 280, and a false-statement penalty under ETA section 281.1 equal to the greater of CAD 4,000 and 15% of the claimed net tax, with additional penalties up to 25% for gross negligence under ITA section 163.2. Criminal prosecution under ETA section 327 and Excise Act, 2001 section 217 for fraudulent zero-rating carries fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment of up to five years; Revenu Québec may additionally claw back QST refunds and cancel the enterprise's NEQ and liquor permit, and CBSA may suspend the importer/exporter license on evidence of diversion of bonded goods into domestic distribution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting under the Bank of Canada Act with supervisory coordination by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for domestic bank conduct and by Global Affairs Canada for federal economic-sanctions administration. Canada maintains no standalone foreign-exchange-control administration analogous to a SAFE regime; FX policy authority is vested in the Currency Act and the Minister of Finance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible across both current-account and capital-account lines. No central-bank permit or prior approval is required for capital contributions, profit repatriation, partnership distributions to non-resident limited partners, or liquidation proceeds. Practical frictions are fiscal and transactional: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (25% statutory, generally treaty-reduced) on remitted partnership distributions, FINTRAC reporting for cross-border electronic-funds transfers and large cash transactions in excess of CAD 10,000, and mandatory screening against OFAC, UN, EU, and federal Canadian sanctions lists. For a Quebec société en commandite (LP), conversion friction arises only from the administrative need to maintain a valid immatriculation number issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and a valid CRA excise-warehouse registration for bonded wine and spirits inventory.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender rules apply. There is no requirement to convert export receipts into CAD, no obligatory repatriation window, and no mandated minimum CAD balance. The Quebec LP may retain USD, EUR, or GBP receipts in foreign-currency operating accounts at domestic Schedule I banks. Residual reporting obligations include: (i) filing under the Statistics Canada / Bank of Canada International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) for cross-border receipts and payments, (ii) FINTRAC EFT transaction reports for transfers over CAD 10,000, and (iii) CRA Form T106/T5013 disclosure for any management fees, commissions, or interest paid to non-residents, together with Part XII.2 investment-partnership rules where passive income is allocable to non-resident partners.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for subscription funds and Operational Multi-Currency Treasury Account (CAD/USD/EUR)
Operational Multi-Currency Account with Global Wire Clearing and Trade Finance Desk
Trade Finance and Commercial Letter of Credit Account (USD/CAD pooling) with Commodity Finance Specialisation
Operational Account with Merchant Clearing and International Treasury Services
Operational Account with Escrow Services and Cross-Border Wire Capabilities
Global Banking Account with Specialised International Trade Desk and Latin American Corridors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary clearing rail; Medium as a secondary disbursement rail only. Canada does not issue electronic-money-institution (EMI) licences; non-resident fintech platforms (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) must register as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC and clear through Canadian Schedule I partner banks. For a Quebec LP engaged in bonded wine and spirits wholesale trade, such platforms cannot support CRA excise-duty payment rails, customs bonded settlements, or UCP 600 documentary credits. Open-account supplier payments below CAD 50,000 may be routed through MSBs, but the principal treasury relationship must remain a licensed Canadian bank for compliance and credit reasons.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Enhanced Due Diligence applies to the Medium_Risk_Enhanced alcohol profile. FINTRAC PCMLTFA permits remote identification, but Schedule I banks typically require a physical or high-grade verified video interview at a commercial banking centre, with the Montreal centre preferred for the Quebec LP, for the General Partner and every authorised signatory. Required documentary items include the certified attestation of immatriculation from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, notarised partnership resolutions, and the executed operating mandate. Limited partners holding 25% or more of capital or profit may be verified remotely through a separate video call but must each provide source-of-wealth declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity in the Quebec limited partnership capital waterfall, including indirect multi-tier limited partners, triggers FINTRAC Enhanced Due Diligence under section 11 of the PCMLTFR and may cause refusal of account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) a certified copy of the partnership agreement (contrat de société) with the capital-commitment schedule, (ii) an ownership-attribution matrix identifying every individual with a direct or indirect 25% or greater economic interest in partnership capital or profit, (iii) the declaration of immatriculation filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, and (iv) source-of-funds statements for each qualifying limited partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded wine/spirits wholesale classification as a high-risk commodity for excise-duty evasion, illicit parallel trade, and trade-based money laundering triggers mandatory enhanced monitoring and possible denial of treasury services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble (i) a valid excise-warehouse licence issued by the Canada Revenue Agency under the Excise Act, 2001 for the bonded premises, (ii) the Quebec liquor authorisation issued by the Régie des alcools du Québec and, where applicable, the SAQ wholesale registration, (iii) CRA excise-duty remittance receipts for all prior removals from bond, and (iv) a full supply-chain due-diligence pack comprising the bonded-warehouse operator's licence, freight forwarder credentials, consignee declarations, and export certificates from the country of origin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wires with third-party payers or intra-group funding present a prohibited third-party payment pattern under FINTRAC guidance, causing payment-velocity and transaction-filtering alarms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) a sworn General Partner declaration explaining the commercial purpose of each third-party remittance, (ii) the underlying purchase order, commercial invoice, and bill of lading referencing the specific container and bond number, (iii) the bank's Third-Party Payment Authorisation Form signed by all authorised signatories, and (iv) a recurring-volume and velocity forecast on a monthly and quarterly basis to pre-clear expected transaction patterns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque national status or multiple residential ties of non-resident limited partners and officers triggers sanctions, PEP, and tax-residency screening failures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (i) certified passport pages and proof of residential address for every General Partner, signatory, and 25%+ limited partner, (ii) tax-residency certificates or Canadian CRA Notices of Assessment for the preceding two tax years for resident signatories, (iii) professional reference letters from the LP's Quebec-registered corporate-services agent, and (iv) a signed sanctions-screening consent permitting OFAC, UN, EU, and UK list checks across all account access points, including API feeds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident capital commitments must be received by SWIFT MT103 with the payment narrative coded 'EQUITY INJECTION - PARTNERSHIP CAPITAL' and the LP immatriculation number as reference, classified per IMF Balance-of-Payments Manual (BPM6) as direct investment into the partnership. The remitter's name on the MT103 must match the LP register exactly; a corporate remitter requires submission of a control-ownership chart proving its LP holding. Funds exceeding CAD 10,000 are reported to FINTRAC and supported by a deposit anticipation letter executed by the General Partner prior to the value date. No Bank of Canada licence or FX conversion approval is required. CAD funds settle over the Lynx high-value system; USD and EUR funds settle via the correspondent nostro accounts of the receiving Schedule I bank. The bank performs a source-of-funds match against the capital-commitment notice for each tranche.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails comprise: (i) SWIFT MT103 open-account transfers and ISO 20022 pain.001 equivalents for supplier settlements relating to Scotch whisky and Bordeaux wine on EXW, FCA, or CFR terms; (ii) commercial sight or usance Letters of Credit issued under UCP 600 and documentary collections under URC 522 for large containerised shipments, with presentation of bills of lading, certificates of origin and age (e.g., Scotch Whisky Association certificate of authenticity, Bordeaux AOC/IGP vintage certificates), and CFIA import/export documentation; (iii) CRA excise-duty payments on removal of product from bond, which must clear exclusively over Canadian payment systems via ACSS or Lynx using the partnership's CRA program account and may not be routed through commercial L/C or MSB rails; and (iv) domestic bonded-warehouse transfers, which settle via Lynx real-time inter-bank transfers and are recorded on the CRA excise-duty schedule.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards with tenors up to 24 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or bank FX Master Agreement, for CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/GBP underlying trade exposures.
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) for matching long-dated supplier payment liabilities, requiring an ISDA Credit Support Annex and a duly adopted General Partner hedging resolution.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to exotic supplier-country currencies (e.g., UAH, MDL) where no deliverable forward market exists; CAD itself is always settled on a deliverable basis, so a CAD NDF is neither permissible nor commercially necessary.
FX spot options and zero-cost collars for open-account receivable and payable cycles, subject to the bank's derivatives-appropriateness review and the LP's documented internal hedging policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD $200 to $2,000; registration may be administratively struck off after two consecutive years of non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year partnerships: March 31; for non-calendar year-end: within 5 months after the fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD $27 per day, up to a maximum of CAD $2,500 for each late T5013 return.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not mandatory for limited partnerships under Quebec law. An audit may be triggered by the partnership agreement, lender covenants, or securities regulation if the LP is a reporting issuer.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE (Canadian GAAP); the partnership may elect ASPE unless consolidated by a public issuer.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The REQ annual declaration must confirm the general partner's identity and any changes to the limited partners' register. Changes in general partnership interests must be filed with the REQ within 30 days. Limited partners' personal details are not publicly disclosed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined statutory headline rate for a general Canadian corporation in Quebec (15% federal + 11.5% provincial); the Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and is not subject to Canadian corporate income tax at the entity level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) benefits from the federal small business deduction, reducing the federal rate to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; Quebec's reduced SME corporate rate is 3.2% on eligible income. For an LP, all income/losses pass through to partners; corporate partners are taxed at combined rates, individual partners at progressive rates. Additional preferential deductions may include the Quebec manufacturing and processing deduction, scientific research and experimental development tax credits, and accelerated capital cost allowance for eligible assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Summary/Slips, filed through Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) My Business Portal / EFILE; Quebec provincial filing is required via Revenu Québec's CLIC or Revenu Québec Online Services, including the provincial partnership information disclosure and Relevé slips.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T5013 return must be filed by the later of March 31 following the calendar year and six months after the partnership's fiscal year-end; for most calendar-year partnerships, the deadline is June 30. Quebec's provincial deadline aligns with CRA for partnerships.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 1 – Partnership Identification / Box 40 Business Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered address, CRA business number, fiscal year end, and jurisdiction of formation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the non-resident partner's representative address and country of residence; ensure the partnership is identified as a Canadian or foreign partnership for tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part 2 – Allocation of Income (Boxes 101–255 / T5013 Summary)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details of gross revenue, cost of goods sold, gross profit, expenses, and net income/loss from the bonded warehouse wholesale trade of aged Scotch and Bordeaux wines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate Canadian-source income to non-resident partners according to the partnership agreement; income allocated must be reported on the T5013 slip. No Part XIII withholding is applied to ordinary business income allocation, but the partner remains taxable in Canada if carrying on a business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec provincial partnership slips reporting the partner's share of income, source deductions, and Quebec tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners not carrying on business in Quebec are generally not required to file a Quebec provincial personal or corporate return, but Quebec may require disclosure where the partner has a permanent establishment in the province.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule of Non-Arms-Length Transactions / Form T106
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all transactions with non-resident related parties, including intercompany purchases of wine/spirits and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Form T106 must be filed for each non-arm's-length transaction with a non-resident where the total value exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in the year; attach transfer pricing documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T5013 filing penalties: CAD 100.00 per day for each return, up to a maximum of CAD 2,500.00 per partnership. For failure to provide a T5013 slip to a partner, penalties are CAD 50.00 per slip, or CAD 100.00 per slip for bulk non-compliance. If the partnership has unpaid Part XIII tax, late filing penalties under section 162 start at 5% plus 1% per month up to 12 months. Gross negligence penalties may be 50% of the understatement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Canadian Income Tax Act for dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident recipient. In the context of a Limited Partnership, the LP itself does not pay dividends; profit allocations flow to partners. Where a corporate structure is used for repatriating LP profits to non-resident investors, the distribution would be characterized as a dividend subject to the 25% statutory rate unless treaty-reduced.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a tax treaty reduction, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the Canadian payer with Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty) along with a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the residence country's tax authority. The payer then applies the reduced rate. For partnership income allocated to a non-resident partner, the partner can assert treaty protection by filing a Canadian non-resident income tax return showing the treaty position and attaching the TRC. CRA and Revenu Québec generally require contemporaneous proof of substance and residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Canadian Part XIII rate: interest 25% (unless exempt as arm's-length interest not dependent on profits), royalties 25% for copyright and industrial royalties. Treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 10% (e.g., US-Canada treaty) and royalties to 0–10% depending on the nature of the IP (US: 0% for copyright, 10% for patents). The Canada–UK treaty similarly reduces interest to 10% and royalties to 0% or 10% depending on type. Withholding relief requires Form NR301 and a TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 – CRA requires the filing of Form T106 and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for each non-arm's-length cross-border transaction or series when the aggregate value of such transactions in a taxation year exceeds CAD 1,000,000. For high-value multinational enterprises, CRA expects a consolidated Master File for transactions of CAD 50 million or more and a Local File for transactions exceeding CAD 1,000,000, although no separate statutory Local/Master File threshold exists in the Income Tax Act.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the manner of the UAE or Bermuda, but substantive economic presence is an implied requirement for treaty entitlement and is enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under section 245 of the Income Tax Act and through judicial doctrines of sham and substance. A Quebec limited partnership engaged in bonded warehouse wholesale trade must maintain physical inventory, qualified staff, decision-making functions, banking, and tax records in Canada; a shell LP with no local substance will attract CRA reassessment, treaty-benefit denial, GAAR penalties, and possible criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting bonded warehouse revenues from wine/spirits sales, fabricating invoices or expenses, or misallocating Canadian profits to a non-resident partner to avoid Canadian income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under section 239(1) of the Income Tax Act, on summary conviction, fines of 50% to 100% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 2 years; on indictment, fines of 100% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years. Civilly, subsection 163(2) imposes a penalty equal to 50% of the unreported tax where false statements or omissions are made knowingly or due to gross negligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are jointly and severally liable under subsection 227.1(1) for taxes withheld but not remitted and for evaded taxes where they participated. CRA can issue a director's liability assessment, garnish personal bank accounts, and, where assets are hidden, apply for travel bans through Federal Court. Limited partners lose their liability shield if they take part in the commercial management of the partnership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting cross-border related-party purchases of Scotch and Bordeaux wines at artificial prices without contemporaneous documentation, or failing to file Form T106 for transactions exceeding CAD 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 247(3) of the Income Tax Act: penalty of 10% of the amount of the net transfer pricing adjustment where the adjustment exceeds CAD 1,000,000, unless the taxpayer made reasonable efforts and prepared contemporaneous documentation. Late T106 filing penalties amount to CAD 100 per day up to CAD 2,500 per occurrence. Reassessed tax will also carry compound interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Insolvency, asset-freeze orders and director liability are available to CRA where the corporate veil is crossed; in LP structures, the general partner becomes personally liable for the partnership's debts, including transfer pricing reassessments, unless it is a shell corporation with no assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a registered office address in Quebec only, with no warehouse, inventory, employees, books, or active management, while routing all commercial activity through a tax-haven entity; or using an LP to strip profits from the Canadian market without real operational capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR under section 245 permits CRA to deny the tax benefits arising from an avoidance transaction; penalties of 50% of the denied benefits may be applied under section 163(2). Revenu Québec can revoke the partnership's registration and impose provincial penalties. Courts may disregard the shell entity under the sham doctrine, and treaty benefits may be rejected under the OECD's principal purpose test.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner may be assessed personally for unpaid taxes and penalties if the corporate form is disregarded. In egregious situations, CRA may issue a 'failure to appear' warrant and freezing orders against the director's personal assets, while travel restrictions are imposed under the Canada Revenue Agency's enforcement powers for serious non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash receipts greater than CAD 10,000 without reporting to FINTRAC, structuring bonded wine/spirits transactions to avoid reporting thresholds, or failing to identify the beneficial owner of a non-resident trust that holds LP interests.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 per violation for failure to report large cash transactions. Criminal Code money-laundering provisions impose imprisonment up to 10 years for laundering proceeds of tax evasion or customs fraud; seizure and forfeiture of assets under the proceeds-of-crime regime are additional sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally prosecutable if they authorized the AML breach; Quebec's anti-money-laundering oversight also applies administrative penalties to both the LP and its officers. Travel bans may be requested by authorities where the person is a principal of a criminal money-laundering network.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting a dividend, interest, royalty, or management fee to a foreign partner or related non-resident entity without deducting the statutory 25% Part XIII withholding tax and without filing the prescribed remittance forms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sections 215 and 227(8) of the Income Tax Act: the payer is liable for the full unreported 25% withholding tax, compounded daily arrears interest, and a 10% penalty on the unremitted amount. CRA may assess the partnership even if the funds have already left Canada and can garnish assets without prior judicial authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Section 227.1 imposes joint and several personal liability on directors and the general partner for all unremitted Part XIII withholding. CRA issues a personal liability certificate, allowing seizure of personal assets; criminal prosecution may follow where the director knowingly participated with the intent to evade the tax, carrying with it imprisonment under section 242.
